segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Hello and welcome to Real Easy English. In this podcast, we have real conversations in easy English to help you understand.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'm Neil.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And I'm Beth. You can watch a video of this podcast and there is a free worksheet on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Hi Beth, how are you?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I'm very well, thank you Neil. How are you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'm good. I tried to watch a film in a foreign language last night.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Oh, interestingly, today we are talking about learning languages.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: We know that everyone listening is learning English and we've both tried to learn some languages, haven't we?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So we're going to be talking about what it's like to learn a language.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Let's start.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: OK. So, Neil, what languages have you tried to learn or what languages can you speak?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well, at school we learned French and also some German, but I don't speak those.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: When I started teaching abroad, I tried to learn the languages in those countries.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So Czech, from the Czech Republic, Spanish and also Japanese.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Ah, very nice, OK.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: How about you?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Well, similar situation.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I learnt French in school I didn really try I didn really enjoy it But when I started teaching I started learning Spanish and I was really motivated So I definitely better at Spanish

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: than I am at French.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Do you find learning languages difficult?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I think that when you start learning a language, it's quite easy because you can learn a lot in a

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: short amount of time. But once you reach that sort of intermediate level, I think it can be

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: very difficult to improve.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yes, it's definitely difficult when you start learning a language

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: and then when you go to that country and try to speak, you realise even if you think you're quite

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: good, that actually you're not so good.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yeah, yeah. What do you think is the hardest thing

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: about learning a new language?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I think listening is very hard, but also speaking because you have to

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: think and concentrate before you say something and then you also then have to think and concentrate

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: to understand the answer and if you get lost you can feel really bad. You can feel embarrassed or

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: awkward or anxious

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yeah I think sometimes you memorize you try to remember words and phrases and then you use them and you feel really good because you said a fluent sentence and then the person replies and you so focused on yes I said something good

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: that you then don't understand what they've said back to you.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Absolutely. Yes. I think everyone studying a language has experienced that.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yeah, definitely. Have you ever done any exams, any tests in a different language?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yes, I have. I've done A-level Spanish. A-level is the school exam you take when you're 18 in the UK.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I did a GCSE in French. That's an exam that we take in school when we're 15, 16 and I failed it.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Oh, no. I'm surprised you've told everybody this.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I know. I don't know why.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Do you have any tips for memorising things? Because when you learn a language, you really have to memorise things.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So I find writing things down and putting them in my house really helps.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And it's about seeing and practicing those words again and again, because the more you say them, the more they get into your head.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah, we get lots of comments from our audience asking how to be more fluent.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: What does that mean?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So fluent is when you able to speak a language without too many pauses We are both English so we can speak English fluently But I can speak Spanish fluently I can speak it okay

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: but I still have to pause and think quite a lot when I speak it.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Let's recap the vocabulary we heard in this conversation, starting with memorise.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Memorise is a verb, which means to learn something until you can remember it.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: We also had exam, which is a test of a student's knowledge.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: If you are fluent in a language, it means you can speak it easily without having to think too much.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And we heard anxious, which means nervous or worried. People are often anxious when

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: they speak a foreign language.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And we've made a brand new series all about how to feel better when you're speaking English.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: There are short videos with tips to help you and longer podcasts about why learning a new

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: language is so difficult. Head to our website to find the latest episodes BBC Learning

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: English.com. And that's it for this episode of Real Easy English. See you soon.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Goodbye.
